name: The Ginkgo of Genko-ji

location.address: Genko-ji, Kotada, Kurose-cho, Higashi-Hiroshima, Hiroshima Prefecture

access: Free. Temple grounds in Kurose-cho Kotada, presumed open in daylight hours like the area's other temples; no gate or restriction found.
transport: No train station in Kurose-cho; reachable by car, roughly 30-40 minutes south of central Saijo.
verify_notes: Report ID 53617, Ministry of Environment giant-tree register, surveyed 2000: girth 3.16m, health good, no age band recorded (不明). Register's own geocoding note calls the coordinate site-level, resolved to the temple itself (Nominatim on facility name), not the trunk, so location_precision stays approximate. Only the register names this specific tree; a second source (e-ohaka.com temple directory) independently confirms Genko-ji exists at this address in Kurose-cho, Kotada 618, but says nothing about a ginkgo. Flagged for that reason: existence and address of the temple are corroborated, the tree itself is registry-only. Web search for a second description of the tree (city bunkazai lists, Hiroshima prefectural greening centre, giant-tree blogs) found nothing. No news or recent survey found confirming it still stands past the 2000 survey; nothing found suggesting it has fallen either. Girth of 3.16m is a genuinely large ginkgo trunk, well clear of the register's 3m floor, and worth recording even without a second voice.

name: The Black Pine of Tokuzen-ji

location.address: Tokuzen-ji, Nora, Toyosaka-cho, Higashi-Hiroshima, Hiroshima Prefecture

access: Free. Temple grounds in Toyosaka-cho Nora, presumed open in daylight hours; no gate or restriction found.
transport: No train or bus stop nearby; reachable by car, rural northern Higashi-Hiroshima.
verify_notes: Report ID 53642, Ministry of Environment giant-tree register, surveyed 2000: girth 3.30m, health good, no age band recorded. Register's own geocoding note calls the coordinate site-level, resolved to the temple itself, not the trunk, so location_precision stays approximate. Only the register names this specific tree; a directory listing (Mapion) independently confirms Tokuzen-ji exists at Toyosaka-cho Nora 289, but says nothing about a pine. Flagged for that reason. Checked the city's Toyosaka-cho cultural-properties page (city.higashihiroshima.lg.jp/.../town/toyosaka/), which lists the town's designated properties (Hongu Hachiman's 1701 hall, the Renkyo-ji Asunaro) and does not mention this pine, so it is registered nationally without a local designation. No news or recent survey found either confirming continued life past 2000 or reporting it felled. Girth of 3.30m is well clear of the register's 3m floor for a black pine, a species usually shaped and tended rather than left to grow wild, which is itself a small sign of a cared-for tree on temple ground.
